Subject: Post-call recap and next steps for PHI deployment options

Thanks Emily and Jonathan — great conversation today. Short recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the audit/compliance asks and the deployment mode trade-offs for PHI workloads:

Summary of requirements we captured
- PHI processing: yes (EHR ingestion + model outputs stored)
- BAA required before any PHI is processed
- Audit log retention: target 24 months (you mentioned 2-year retention)
- Encryption: customer-managed keys preferred for some data at rest
- SOC 2 evidence is required for procurement team review

Deployment modes discussed
- Hosted API: fastest to start, but does not meet BAA + customer KMS requirement for PHI (not acceptable per call)
- Dedicated capacity: provides isolated GPU pools, predictable throughput, and we can restrict tenancy; supports our standard BAA and audit logs
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full network isolation, customer-managed KMS/HSM, best for strict regulatory controls and on-prem audit workflows

Immediate asks from your side
- Confirm preferred deployment mode (Dedicated vs Private) for scoping SOW
- Confirm final list of compliance artifacts procurement needs (SOC2 + any additional questionnaire)
- Procurement contact to receive BAA and SOC2: I’ve CC'd a procurement mailbox below in follow ups if needed

Attachments I’m sharing in this message (stubs)
- BAA_template.docx (editable)
- Redwood_Security_Pack_v3.pdf (overview + redaction guidance)

Proposed next steps
1) We’ll send the redacted SOC2 + security pack (attached) and BAA template by EOD.
2) Neha (cc) will schedule a 30m technical checklist call to validate network/KMS/logging requirements if you choose Dedicated or Private.
3) We’ll provide a pricing estimate for 50 req/s baseline (Dedicated) vs Private (network/on-prem costs) and a draft SOW.

If you can confirm preferred deployment mode and procurement contact, we’ll prioritize the SOW and procurement packet.

Thanks again,

Hi Emily — quick answers and more detail below. I’m copying Neha so she can follow up with a technical checklist call.

Latency / SLAs
- Dedicated: with a pinned GPU pool and our low-latency routing, we routinely meet sub-200ms 95th for 512-token hits for production models at the 50rps range (assuming typical batch sizing and KV cache behavior). We’ll provide model/profile-specific numbers once we know model size and seq-length distribution.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): latency depends on network topology; when co-located in-app region or private colo the network hop is eliminated and latency can be similar or slightly better than Dedicated. If you place inference off-site, you may add variability.

Log retention
- Redwood supports configurable retention policies for audit logs (events, API call traces, model inference metadata). 24-month retention is supported; for Private VPC we can arrange local retention policies or export hooks to your storage.

Attached: redacted SOC2 report and a compliance mapping that ties artifacts to typical procurement questionnaire items.

Proposed timeline (if you confirm Dedicated)
- Day 0: Sign BAA (we can start redaction now)
- Day 3-7: Technical checklist call + network certs exchange
- Week 2: Provision dedicated pool (staging) and initial smoke tests
- Week 3-4: Cutover and go-live (depends on model onboarding time)

If you lean Private, timeline expands by 1–3 weeks depending on network/KMS procurement and on-prem logistics.

Attachments: SOC2-Report-Redwood-2024-redacted.pdf, Compliance-Mapping-Checklist.xlsx (stubs)

Would you like Neha to book a 30m slot tomorrow to run through the checklist?

Best,
